summary: Del Norte County lookout tower on Little Rattlesnake Mountain, built 1935. Gone by the 1977 USGS recovery note; firelookout.org also lists it as gone. No later source found.

facts.design: Wooden tower, painted white, about 14 feet square at the top, with a small garage and store shed about 150 feet east (1941 Coast and Geodetic Survey description)
facts.status_note: The 1977 USGS recovery note says the tower no longer exists. firelookout.org also lists the site as gone. No later source we read describes the site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts lists the site under the Siskiyou National Forest, then the Six Rivers National Forest. Peakbagging lists Six Rivers. The 1930s-40s records name Siskiyou.

notes_for_editor: Gone status is well supported by the 1977 USGS recovery note and the firelookout.org row (type Tower, status Gone, no register number). Thin on everything else: the 1935 build date comes from a 1939 history quoted second-hand on Forest Lookouts. The forest name differs across sources. An earlier draft gave FFLOS US 687, CA 10, which belongs to Ranger Peak (Riverside County), so it was removed. 'Only' was dropped from the Six Rivers claim because the full Peakbagging table was not checked. No source describes the site today or its access.
